mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a recession.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in housing starts (HOUST) above their 12-month moving average signals weakening consumer demand but expanding housing investment, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as construction-related equities outperform.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive (> 0%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent when unemployment exceeds 7%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months, or the effect reverses during periods of strong GDP growth (> 4% q/q).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a broad-based contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of rising consumer confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary shock, which increases uncertainty and risk premia, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months, or the effect is absent when GDP growth exceeds 3% q/q.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average while personal income growth (proxied by PAYEMS growth) slows signals a shift from spending to saving, which reduces aggregate demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month MA AND PAYEMS growth < 0% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent when consumer confidence is rising.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the labor force participation rate (implied by UNRATE dynamics) above its 5-year average without a corresponding rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals an increase in slack, which depresses wage growth and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 5-year average AND PAYEMS growth < 0% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during periods of strong GDP growth (> 4% q/q).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average with no corresponding rise in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) signals a housing-led demand expansion without broad price pressures, which supports construction and materials equities and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month MA AND CPIAUCSL growth < 0.1% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (> 0%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent when mortgage rates rise above 6%.
